the_one_page_injector_spec.title: C5' — repair is injector semantics: a one-page spec, run for the first time
the_one_page_injector_spec.injector_identity: EXTERNAL HARNESS ACTION (not a kernel primitive): a harness-side byte-write pass between ticks (the E-Q5 setCell path verbatim: sub[y*w+x] = packByte(2, 55) on every ring cell). The kernel stays untouched: tick() cannot repair (tau is immutable in tick; d moves only by neighborhood pressure — there is no repair term to find), which is exactly why an injector must live outside tick for 'repair' to be meaningful. The guest's round-6 open question 'external harness vs kernel primitive' is answered: harness; a kernel-primitive injector would be a NEW kernel capability and is out of scope for the one-page run.
the_one_page_injector_spec.injection_budget: Exactly ONE application per injected trial, applied once between t=50 and t=51 (E-Q5's INJECT_AT=50 path verbatim). Cost accounting receipted per trial: |ring| cell-writes per application (RING_N computed in-run), 1 application, budget-0 = the no-injector arms (A0 pristine, A1 damaged). No partial or repeated injections.
the_one_page_injector_spec.what_repair_means: 'Repair' is DEFINED as injector-mediated restoration of ring d-bytes (tau never changes anywhere). Substrate self-repair would be integrity increasing without an injector application — the falsifier's first branch.
the_one_page_injector_spec.falsifier_verbatim: any admissible trial where integrity increases WITHOUT an injector application (substrate self-repair), or where repairTick is non-null, or where post-injection re-erosion is non-monotone — any one of these kills C5' as stated and forces a rewrite of the injector one-pager
